paper_metadata.title: Effect of rotary swaging and annealing on mechanical properties and microstructure evolution of aeroengine high-temperature alloy steel tube
paper_metadata.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology

evidence.quote: Rotary swaging (RS) with mandrel was performed on aeroengine high-temperature alloy steel tubes at room temperature.
AM355 stainless steel is an important high-temperature alloy steel because of its high strength and corrosion resistance [9].
In this study, RS and annealing experiments of the aeroengine high-temperature alloy steel tubes were carried out.

Φ20.5 mm rods were initially cut from the AM355 rod by wire-electrode cutting.
Deep hole drilling was then conducted to create an inner hole with a diameter of Φ10 mm.
A mandrel was used during the RS process to form an inner-stepped hole with a diameter of Φ8 mm. The RS process reduced the outer diameter to Φ17.75 mm.
Tubes after RS were then heat-treated at 700 ℃, 800 ℃, and 900 ℃ in a furnace for 100 min, followed by air cooling.

Compared to the initial condition, accumulation of dislocations occurred after RS due to cold plastic deformation.
Annealing below 900 ℃ triggered substantial recovery of the material, gradually eliminating the accumulated dislocations.
Dislocations introduced by RS showed noticeable recovery at 800 °C, although the martensite structure remained visible.
At 900 ℃ , significant recrystallization occurs in RS tubes, leading to the replacement of the martensite structure with recrystallized fine grains.
Annealing at 900 ℃ caused significant decomposition of martensite blocks, resulting in their shortening and coarsening.
The FCC γ-Fe, BCC α-Fe, and Cr2N phases were tested and Fig. 12 shows the fraction of the FCC phase and Cr2N phase.
The FCC phase content of the 25-AP condition was evidently higher compared to other conditions, reaching 3.47%, which could be considered residual austenite.
It was interesting the RS tubes exhibited higher Cr2N phase content
annealing after RS further reduced the residual FCC phase to less than 0.2%

attributes.morphology: long and continuous laths within prior austenite grain boundaries

evidence.quote: Martensite lath structures in prior austenite grain boundaries (GBs) could be observed under all conditions except 900-RS.
Under 900-AP condition, no recrystallization happened and the martensite lath structures underwent a transition from long and continuous morphology to short and coarse, discontinuous morphology.

attributes.morphology: fine equiaxed grains uniformly distributed in each prior grain

evidence.quote: Under the 900-RS condition, the martensite structures were eliminated and replaced by fine recrystallized grains. The prior austenite grains mainly had a radius of about 20 ~ 30 µm and the new recrystallized grains only owned a radius of less than 8 µm.
For RS tubes, shear layers were produced in the near outer surface area and the thickness was around 145 µm, 105 µm, 100 µm, and 70 µm, respectively, at 25-RS, 700-RS, 800-RS, and 900-RS states.

On the inner surface of the tubes, some dense compressed layers of grains were observed. The shearing of the grains in the layer near the inner surface was not pronounced.
A large number of dimples were distributed in all fracture surfaces, indicating that the fracture was dominated by ductile fracture mode in all states.
